# F-015 L2a, ~1.5 minutes. Expect: a rocket drawn as a rocket and a train as a train (test31: "a rocket is a car");
# rain falling vertically at 3 m/s and a man walking at 4 m/s: umbrella tilt 53.1° forward, rain seen by the man 5 m/s,
# streaks slanted when seen by the man; a river 100 m wide at 3 m/s and a boat at 5 m/s: shortest time 20 s, drift
# 60 m, then straight opposite: heading 36.9° upstream, 25 s; two trains 200 m apart at 20 and 30 m/s: meet in 4 s.
@setup subject=Physics grade=11 topic="Relative velocity"

Today we will look at relative velocity.
[pause 1]
Imagine a rocket moving at a speed of 100 metres per second and a train moving at 30 metres per second.
[pause 3]
Let's get back to the slides.
[pause 1.5]
Imagine rain falling vertically at 3 metres per second, and a man walking at 4 metres per second.
[pause 3]
How does the rain look to the man?
[pause 3]
Let's get back to the slides.
[pause 1.5]
Imagine a river 100 metres wide flowing at 3 metres per second, and a boat that moves at 5 metres per second heading straight across.
[pause 3.5]
Now the boat wants to reach the point straight opposite.
[pause 3]
Let's get back to the slides.
[pause 1.5]
Imagine two trains 200 metres apart running towards each other at 20 metres per second and 30 metres per second.
[pause 3.5]
Let's get back to the slides.
[pause 2]
